attribution.note: Marcus's own hot take in his newsletter; endorsed.

semantics.note: In context the line refers to Grok 3; 'magically' is emphasis. Present-state observation that hallucinations persist.

contract.note: Plain reading (Grok 3 still fabricates facts/URLs at launch) is ordinary and fair; launch-version scope is reasonable.

evidence.note: Karpathy's launch-day early-access test reports hallucinated nonexistent URLs and incorrect factual claims in Grok 3 DeepSearch.

reviews.rationale: Direct contemporaneous testing of the launch product documents fabricated URLs and false factual assertions, meeting the support condition. No evidence suggests fabrication was eliminated.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Correctly drops the speculative access explanation; keeps the no-full-o3 comparison and handful-of-benchmarks assertions.

contract.note: Limiting to the public launch presentation and counting benchmark families is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous Feb 18 post notes o3 was omitted from the livestream chart. Poster is OpenAI staff, but this is an observation of xAI's chart, not self-disclosure.
Summary from a day later names three benchmark families (AIME, GPQA, LiveCodeBench) and lists o3-mini, not full o3, among the competitors.

reviews.rationale: Launch comparisons excluded full o3 and centred on three benchmark families, satisfying both parts of the support condition. The xAI article with broader tables came later and is outside scope.

semantics.note: Isolates the present-tense moat clause; the price and profit forecasts are handled separately.

contract.note: Reading moat as capability lead over rival models fits the context of competing-model comparisons; the flag that interpretation matters is honest.

evidence.note: On Feb 18 LMArena announced early Grok 3 at #1 overall, above OpenAI models. The same page shows DeepSeek-R1 matching o1 in January.
January company-reported parity of DeepSeek-R1 with o1; preceding trend, outside target period.

reviews.rationale: Under the capability reading, rivals were reaching or passing OpenAI models: Grok 3 led Arena at launch, following R1's parity with o1. The evidence doesn't cover broader business moats, which the contract fairly excludes.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'will continue' forecast with the 'so' causal link preserved; profit clause excluded.

contract.note: Requiring a renewed multi-provider price-cut episode tied to comparable rivals is a fair, not stretched, reading of 'so price wars will continue'.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure of a June 2025 o3 price cut; confirms a price change but not its cause.
DeepSeek Sept 2025 cut of 50%+ with a replacement model; credits efficiency, so weak on causation.
Sept 2026 report: OpenAI cut prices to compete with Anthropic/Google, and the big labs cut prices for months under pressure from comparable open models.

reviews.rationale: Independent reporting dated before the evaluation date documents renewed price cuts across several providers, explicitly linked to comparable rival offerings. That meets the early-resolution rule. DeepSeek's efficiency explanation weakens only that one item.
